Browne Amplification browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal Browne Amplification Alkene - Nashville Drive Published on February 24, 2026 Browne Amplification overdrive pedal Information The Browne Amplification Alkene Nashville Drive is a compact overdrive pedal designed to deliver the organic, touch-sensitive response associated with classic "Nashville" overdrives found on the pedalboards of session guitarists such as Tim Pierce and Jerry McPherson. Introduced as the successor to the discontinued Atom Nashville Drive, the Alkene occupies the same compact green enclosure but represents a distinct circuit and tonal direction within the Browne lineup. The Atom, formerly the standalone version of the green channel from the Browne Protein Dual Overdrive, was discontinued in February 2025. Its retirement was intended to eliminate overlap with the Protein Dual Overdrive and preserve the exclusivity of that circuit. While the Atom delivered a refined, Nobels ODR-1-style op-amp overdrive with a transparent voice and tight low end, the Alkene replaces it with a newly developed drive circuit offering expanded tonal flexibility and a different gain structure. At its core, the Alkene combines musical clipping with gentle, amp-like compression, engineered to provide a familiar Nashville-style feel with greater control. The overall gain range has been deliberately lowered to ensure that the entire sweep of the Gain control remains usable. Key mid frequencies have been restored to avoid an overly scooped response, and the low end has been tightened for clarity and punch. The result is an overdrive that reinforces low-mid body without becoming muddy, maintaining high touch sensitivity and dynamic response. The Alkene is designed to excel in crunchy rhythm applications where chord clarity is essential, while also producing singing, expressive lead tones when driven harder. It responds notably well to guitar volume adjustments, offering effective clean-up and dynamic control. One of its defining traits is its ability to enhance thin or stiff backline amplifiers by adding low-mid warmth and a subtle sag that improves feel and responsiveness.
